story: The buffalo demon Mahishasura won a boon that no man or god could kill him, and drove the gods out of heaven. The combined anger and power of the gods took shape as Durga, armed with each god's weapon. She fought him for nine days and nights and killed him on the tenth.
belief: Her victory is celebrated every year in Navaratri and Durga Puja, especially in Bengal, and on Vijayadashami. Devotees see her as the invincible mother who protects the good.
turns: The gods' own carelessness made her necessary: Mahishasura's boon left out women, because he never imagined a woman could defeat him. In some tellings her rage in battle grew so great that it gave birth to Kali.
facts: Durga Puja in Kolkata is on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Her name means 'the one who is difficult to reach', the invincible.
The Devi Mahatmya, about 1,500 years old, is the main text that tells her story.
